use-ai-to-write-emails.title: Write a polite email with AI
transcript: A blank email can be harder than the email itself. Imagine you need to move an appointment. Start with the purpose and the tone.
Write a short, polite email asking to move my appointment to next week. Leave the name and date as placeholders.
Check the draft for promises or details you never gave. Replace the placeholders yourself and read the message once before you send it.
Try it with the guide at Spinnit dot site.

use-ai-to-write-emails.title: Make an AI draft sound more like you
transcript: Suppose an AI thank-you note sounds stiff. Decide what you would actually say, then ask for a small rewrite with one real detail you are comfortable sharing.
Rewrite this as two short, friendly sentences. Keep the thank-you for helping with the garden. Use everyday words and add no new details.
Read it out loud. If a phrase feels unlike you, swap it for your own words. You can use the draft as a starting point and write the last line yourself.
Try it with the guide at Spinnit dot site.

everyday-ai-prompts.title: Turn a club notice into a checklist
everyday-ai-prompts.practice: Check each item against the notice.
transcript: A long notice can hide the one thing you need to do. Try this with an invented gardening club notice, or with a public notice that has no personal details.
Turn this notice into a checklist. Separate what I need to bring, what I need to do, and any dates mentioned. If a detail is missing, say so.
Put the checklist next to the notice. If the checklist says to bring gloves, find the sentence about gloves. Use the original notice to confirm the date.
Try it with the guide at Spinnit dot site.

everyday-ai-prompts.title: Get AI to compare two options
transcript: Imagine choosing between two invented hobby classes. One is close by on a Tuesday. The other is on Saturday, a little farther away. Give AI those details and say what matters to you.
Compare these two classes in a table. Show day, travel and cost. Use only the details I give you. Mark missing details as unknown.
Look for gaps in the table. If you never gave a price, leave it unknown until you can ask the organiser.
Try it with the guide at Spinnit dot site.

everyday-ai-prompts.title: Turn a vague prompt into a usable plan
everyday-ai-prompts.practice: One drawer. Twenty minutes. Three steps.
transcript: Try asking for a weekend tidying plan. A long reply might assume you have a whole afternoon. Give the assistant a smaller job you can actually start.
Give me a twenty-minute plan to tidy one kitchen drawer. Use things I already have. Give me three steps and tell me where to start.
If the plan starts with sorting the entire kitchen, remind the assistant of the one-drawer limit. Try the first step and adjust the rest to suit you.
Try it with the guide at Spinnit dot site.

how-to-ask-ai-follow-up-questions.title: Get a simpler explanation from AI
transcript: Suppose an answer says to sync your files. If that word is new to you, ask about that one part in the same conversation.
Explain what syncing means in two sentences. Use an example with a phone and a tablet. Keep any technical words out.
If the example still feels fuzzy, ask what happens when you change the file on your phone. Keep the follow-up focused on the part you want to understand.
Try it with the guide at Spinnit dot site.

useful-things-ai-can-do.title: Practise a phone call with AI
useful-things-ai-can-do.practice: Practise one question at a time.
transcript: If a phone call makes you nervous, try a dry run. Imagine calling a library to ask about joining. Use made-up details while you practise.
Pretend you work at a library. Help me practise asking how to join. Ask me one question at a time, then give me one tip.
Try the conversation again using that tip. When you are ready to make the real call, ask the library for its actual joining requirements.
Try it with the guide at Spinnit dot site.

useful-things-ai-can-do.title: Ask for one step at a time
useful-things-ai-can-do.practice: Say “I’m ready” when you want the next step.
transcript: A page of instructions can feel like too much. Imagine you want to organise a shelf. Ask the assistant to give you one small action and then wait.
Help me organise one shelf. Give me the first step only. Wait for me to say I am ready before giving me the next step.
Do the first action. If something about the shelf changes the plan, explain that before asking for the next step. You can stop whenever you have done enough.
Try it with the guide at Spinnit dot site.

what-not-to-share-with-ai.title: What to leave out of an AI prompt
transcript: Imagine asking AI for a parcel enquiry. The draft needs to say the parcel has not arrived. It can use a placeholder for the tracking number and address.
Draft a short message about a parcel that has not arrived. Use placeholders for my name, address and tracking number.
Add any necessary details yourself in the message you send to the delivery company. Keep passwords and one-time codes out of the chat.
Try it with the guide at Spinnit dot site.

how-to-check-ai-answers.title: Check a date AI gives you
how-to-check-ai-answers.practice: Confirm the date with the organiser.
transcript: Imagine an AI answer tells you a garden club meeting is on Thursday. Before adding it to your diary, open the club's current notice or contact the organiser.
Which source is that date from? Show me the original notice and say if you cannot find it.
Open the source yourself. Look for the date, year and location. If the notice is old or two pages disagree, ask the organiser before making plans.
Try it with the guide at Spinnit dot site.
